decisions.reason: The deterministic coefficient pairing extends to every H(delta), delta>0, but the white-noise observation clause requires delta>1/2. Added that restriction only to the experiment clause. The trace criterion and local Gaussian realization justify this domain; the weighted Cauchy–Schwarz extension and all existing valid observation uses are preserved.

Read Section 3.2, equations (19)–(25), and Theorem 3 (PDF pp.12–14). Equation (24) permits Gaussian prior parameters with alpha>1/2; Theorem 3 requires alpha>1 for both S cases. Corrected the attribution while preserving the separate local Gaussian alpha>1/2 regime and all prior constructions.

F1 omitted the weight-one Haar scaling coordinate. Corrected the norm to max(|x_*|,D(x)) and explicitly included that coordinate in the Cauchy limit, rational approximants and l2 bound. Detail tails and coarse-retaining projections then prove the unchanged Statement. This finite-coordinate omission was nonfatal to the underlying weighted-c0 argument.

F4 inaccurately described Markov’s interface. It now states P(Y>=a)<=EY/a and derives its exponential application. Step 3.1 already correctly bounds the log-mgf, chooses lambda=x/(V+bx), and obtains both tails. Checked the Gamma transformation, grouped transforms, AC and zero-variance case; the Statement and proof remain unchanged.

Made n>=1 explicit in the Example and verification, avoiding the undefined n=0 expression. The Hilbert-space expansion gives derivative 2<1,h> and remainder ||h||_2^2; the chosen perturbations have scaled remainder exactly one. This domain clarification changes no conclusion and does not assert that a posterior meets the supplier’s contraction premise.

F2 invoked calibration without asserting its hypotheses. Added all calibration hypotheses at 0<alpha<1, including bounded positive truth, primitive summability, posterior BvM, sampling-center CLT and continuous locally unique positive norm quantiles. These justify coverage and R_n^M=O_P(1). The wavelet low/high split and geometric sums then establish the unchanged diameter rate.

Replaced the unscaled CDF posterior claim by the posterior law of sqrt(n)(F_f-F_Tn) on C([0,1]) in sampling probability. The S/H posterior and sampling limits use identical centers and bridge covariance; positivity and summability verify norm quantiles. Those verified premises also meet the repaired diameter theorem. Corrected misleading original-range wording in step 1.1.
